folks.name: Josh Miller
folks.label: Sold his first company, Branch, to Facebook; worked in the Obama White House; invested at Thrive Capital; then founded The Browser Company, creators of Arc and Dia. Its core doctrine is to treat software as personal art and optimize for how an interface feels rather than what an analytics dashboard can measure.

startHere.label: The Ev Williams story: “No one has any idea”
startHere.context: On meeting Twitter co-founder Ev Williams and learning why everyone in tech is making it up as they go along.

passages.text: We were a web browser company that pretended it was a consumer company that made behind the scenes YouTube videos and got really excited when we made the Spotify icon.
One of the best compliments I think I ever received about our work was someone was like, I don’t know how you’re going to beat Chrome, but you seem like you’re having a lot of fun.

Beware of anyone you meet in Silicon Valley that purports to have the answers to all the questions. Because all of us who had made something like Twitter know we were all making it up as we went along.

folks.name: Nashilu Mouen-Makoua
folks.role: Storyteller & Writer · The Browser Company alumna
folks.thesis: Third places, physical presence, and the living internet.
folks.label: Born in South London, based in Brooklyn, and previously an investor at First Round Capital, Nashilu Mouen-Makoua served as Head of Storytelling at The Browser Company. Her observational documentary work explores internet culture through the tactile, hyper-local spaces where humans gather to share connection and digital life.

startHere.label: Hyper-local spaces for regulars only
startHere.context: Field inquiry into why people still travel to physical internet cafes when connectivity is everywhere.

passages.talkTitle: Inside the Secret World of NYC’s Last Internet Cafes
passages.text: When the internet is anywhere and everywhere, why do you go to one place? These are hyper-local spaces designed to serve specific people in specific neighborhoods with specific use cases, wants, and desires. These are spaces for regulars and regulars only.

passages.talkTitle: Inside the Secret World of NYC’s Last Internet Cafes
passages.text: These simple rooms reflect the neighborhoods they were built for and prompt us to reconsider how we think about the internet and what we take for granted.
